abstraction_design.rationale: The abstractions (Section, CardList, MovesTable, format helpers, pokeapi/data/server layering) cover the app's real variation and would absorb an Items section with mostly new code, not copied code. Deductions for the repeated route boilerplate across detail pages and the home page's parallel card-data shape.

findings.issue: The home page builds card data through a parallel path (HomeSpecies built inline) instead of the shared cardsFromPokemonRefs/CardData builder, so sprite, alt-form and ordering fixes must be applied twice (data.ts:83 and data.ts:153).
findings.suggestion: Have buildHomeData reuse cardsFromPokemonRefs (or a shared species-card builder) and attach types/generation to CardData, so every list of Pokémon cards has one derivation path.

findings.issue: The loader → null-check → notFound() → head-title pattern is copy-pasted across all four detail routes (moves/$name.tsx:6-17, abilities/$name.tsx:6-12, types/$name.tsx:6-12, pokemon/$name.tsx:9-17); adding each new resource type copies ~12 lines of boilerplate.
findings.suggestion: Extract a small helper (e.g. detailRouteOptions({ serverFn, param }) or a shared pageTitle/head factory) so new resource routes only declare what differs.

findings.issue: Table body cells are hardcoded separately from the column definitions (COLUMNS at line 14, columnValue at line 21), so adding or reordering a column requires three synchronized edits inside one component.
findings.suggestion: Drive both <thead> and <tbody> from the single columns array (with a per-column render function).

findings.issue: CardList's typesByName Map<string, ...> prop exists solely so the home page can pass type data keyed by species name — an implicit coupling between CardList and one caller.
findings.suggestion: Carry types on the card data itself (CardData.types) so CardList has a single flat contract.

findings.issue: Hash navigation (#moves) is handled by a hand-rolled useEffect with rAF and a 150 ms setTimeout fallback rather than the router's scroll restoration.
findings.suggestion: Enable scrollRestoration on the router (app/src/router.tsx:5) and remove the timing-based workaround, or centralize this in the root so other anchor targets benefit too.

findings.issue: The 'omit empty/default params' rule is implemented twice — in validateSearch and again in buildSearch (index.tsx:38-46) — so a new filter parameter must be threaded through both.
findings.suggestion: Derive buildSearch (and the filter controls) from a single declarative filter schema.

findings.issue: Section derives the heading id from the heading text, so two same-named sections on one page would produce duplicate ids and broken aria-labelledby targets.
findings.suggestion: Require an explicit id (it is passed everywhere already) instead of falling back to a text-derived slug.

findings.issue: The NotFound component sets document.title inside a client-only useEffect, so the SSR title for unmatched URLs differs from the declarative head() convention used by every other page.
findings.suggestion: Use the root route's head() (or a notFound head hook) to declare the title like the rest of the app.

findings.issue: API records are handled as untyped any throughout the builders, so renaming a field or adding an endpoint requires re-reading raw data shapes with no compiler help.
findings.suggestion: Add a small api-types.ts with the record shapes actually consumed (species, pokemon, move, ability, type), at least for the fields used.

findings.issue: loaderDeps: () => ({}) is a no-op; it adds noise without changing the loader's dependency behavior.
findings.suggestion: Delete the line (the default is already empty deps).

summary: This is a well-layered TanStack Start app: server-only data access, a server-function seam, and presentational shared components mean most changes land in one predictable file. The two real editability costs are the home page's parallel card-data path (fixes must be made twice) and the copy-pasted detail-route boilerplate that every new resource section will duplicate. I'd approve it with the card-builder unification and a shared route helper as follow-ups.
